the skill's own scripts/ directory on disk

classes: linked ./scripts/<file> exists beside the SKILL.md -> no error (R3)
linked ./scripts/<file> absent -> error naming the skill relative path and the script path (R1)
bare scripts/<file> link form, same two outcomes — the AC lists both spellings (R2)
link target outside scripts/ (../other/x.mjs, ../../root.md) -> out of scope for this producer, owned by checkLinks (R4 + control R16)

non-checkable target under scripts/ — placeholder (/[<>{}*[\]]/, line 218), pattern path (NNN/YYYY, line 219), URL scheme, absolute, anchor — filtered by isCheckableTarget, and a '#fragment' suffix stripped as checkLinks does at line 227 -> no error (R19)

the delegation is load-bearing, not assumed: R19 and R20 fail any producer that scans the raw body or matches raw targets instead of reusing extractLinkTargets / isCheckableTarget / fragment stripping (the real corpus cannot discriminate — it holds exactly two scripts/ link targets, both plain, both existing)

inventory.producer: checkSkillLocalScripts(skillsDir, installedSkillsDir) — the mirror half; naming transform '<category>/<name>' -> 'pair-<category>-<name>' per transformPath(SKILL_COPY_OPTS) / installedArtifactPath in skill-md-mirror.ts
inputs: every regular file under packages/knowledge-hub/dataset/.skills/<category>/<name>/scripts/, RECURSIVELY — sub-directories included: the bounded flatten (flattenDepth 2) preserves the third and deeper segments, so `workflow/alpha/scripts/lib/util.mjs` really installs as `pair-workflow-alpha/scripts/lib/util.mjs` (verified by running the real installedArtifactPath at this head). A nested script ships, therefore it is guarded; the directory entry itself is walked, never read as a file.
its twin under .claude/skills/pair-<category>-<name>/scripts/<same sub-path> (installed root resolved by the module, per the card: resolve(ROOT,'..','..','.claude','skills'))
representations: report line in RunResult.errors naming BOTH paths and the kind (missing | drifted)
consumers: pair update (the copy pipeline that produces the derived copy)
classes: twin present and byte-identical -> no error (R7)
twin missing -> error naming both paths, kind 'missing' (R5)
twin differs by >=1 byte (same length included) -> error naming both paths, kind 'drifted' (R6, R7)
installed skills root absent (dataset-only checkout) -> twin check skipped, no error (R10)
installed twin with no dataset source (orphan) -> ignored, no error (R8)
unreadable script path (I/O error on read) -> error naming the path, never a silent 'identical' (R11)
bare/meta skill at depth 1 owning a scripts/ sub-directory -> refused: the bounded flatten cannot install it (R12)
script nested in a scripts/ sub-directory, twin missing -> error naming both mirrored nested paths, kind 'missing' (R21)
script nested in a scripts/ sub-directory, twin present and identical -> no error, and no EISDIR on the sub-directory entry (R22)
interactions: the real corpus is the cross-product that must stay clean: 10 dataset skill-local scripts across 6 workflow skills, all byte-identical to their installed twins at the base head, and all flat — so the recursion class is decided by R21/R22 alone, never by the corpus (R14 stays green either way)
runChecks must call the producer against the REAL installed root, so a drifted dataset script fails the gate end to end (R13)

R12 and R21 share the flatten authority and pull in opposite directions: `next/scripts/router.mjs` installs as `pair-next-scripts/router.mjs` (a SEPARATE top-level skill dir — verified at this head), which is why the depth-1 layout is refused, whereas `workflow/alpha/scripts/lib/util.mjs` stays inside the skill and is therefore guarded rather than refused

The CLI is spawned from a copy of the production module in a temp ROOT, which is what defeats the hard-coded SKILLS_DIR at line 58 without any production edit; stdout is asserted so a crash cannot masquerade as the FAIL branch. AC-3 class 2 reworded from 'existing behavior, unchanged' to an actively guarded class.

closed by DECIDING the class recursive, on evidence: installedArtifactPath maps a nested scripts/lib/util.mjs inside the skill, so a nested script ships and must be guarded — 'ignored' would leave a shipped artifact unguarded, so the 'prove it does not throw' alternative does not apply. AC-2 inputs now state recursion explicitly, and an AC-2 interaction records that R12 and R21 read the same flatten authority in opposite directions.
